library(shiny)
library(sfsmisc)
library(qgam)
source("dharma.R")

lab <- c(ok    = "No assumptions violated",
         over  = "Overdispersion",
         under = "Underdispersion",
         zero  = "Zero-inflation",
         curve = "Non-linearity",
         out   = "Outlier")

fl <- c(poisson = "Poisson", binomial = "binomial (10 trials)")

w <- lapply(list(poisson = c(over = 2, under = 2, zero = 2, curve = 2, out = 2),
                 binomial = c(over = 2, under = 2, curve = 2, out = 2)), function(w) c(ok = sum(w) / 3, w))
lam <- 2

scen <- function(s, fam) {
  set.seed(s)
  sample(names(w[[fam]]), 1, prob = w[[fam]])
}

N <- 200

dif <- list(
  poisson = rbind(
    over  = c(Easy = 3.6, Medium = 6.6, Hard = 12.4, Impossible = 32),
    under = c(3.27, 2.41, 1.82, 1.36),
    zero  = c(0.235, 0.147, 0.075, 0.03),
    curve = c(1.32, 0.976, 0.581, 0.15),
    out   = c(1e-4, 1e-3, 6e-3, 0.05)),
  binomial = rbind(
    over  = c(Easy = 0.227, Medium = 0.16, Hard = 0.105, Impossible = 0.057),
    under = c(3.27, 2.41, 1.82, 1.36),
    curve = c(2.65, 1.89, 1.2, 0.39),
    out   = c(1e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2))
)

mu <- function(x, fam, type = "ok", lvl = "Easy", d = 1) {
  e <- if (type %in% c("curve", "zero")) dif[[fam]][type, lvl] else 0
  h <- if (type == "curve") d * e * (x^2 - 1 / 3) else 0
  m <- if (fam == "poisson") exp(log(40) / 2 + log(10) / 2 * x + h) else plogis(qlogis(0.85) * x + h)
  if (type == "zero") (1 - e) * m else m
}

ks <- function(fam) if (fam == "poisson") 0:200 else 0:10

cmd <- function(m, nu, fam) {
  k <- ks(fam)
  ck <- if (fam == "poisson") -lfactorial(k) else lchoose(10, k)
  if (fam == "binomial") m <- 10 * m
  nu <- rep_len(nu, length(m))
  vapply(seq_along(m), function(i) {
    p <- function(t) {
      l <- t * k + nu[i] * ck
      exp(l - max(l))
    }
    q <- p(uniroot(function(t) sum(k * p(t)) / sum(p(t)) - m[i], c(-30, 40), extendInt = "yes", tol = 1e-12)$root)
    q / sum(q)
  }, as.numeric(k))
}

qcm <- function(u, m, nu, fam) colSums(apply(cmd(m, nu, fam), 2, cumsum) < rep(u, each = length(ks(fam))))

sim <- function(n, fam, type, lvl = "Easy") {
  e  <- if (type != "ok") dif[[fam]][type, lvl]
  x  <- runif(N, -1, 1)
  uy <- runif(N)
  ub <- runif(N)
  uz <- runif(N)
  d  <- if (runif(1) < 0.5) -1 else 1
  if (type == "out") {
    x[1] <- d
    uy[1] <- if (fam == "binomial" && d > 0) e else 1 - e
  }
  m <- mu(x, fam, if (type == "curve") type else "ok", lvl, d)
  y <- switch(type,
              over  = if (fam == "poisson") qnbinom(uy, e, mu = m) else
                qbinom(uy, 10, qbeta(ub, m * (1 - e) / e, (1 - m) * (1 - e) / e)),
              under = qcm(uy, m, e, fam),
              zero  = ifelse(uz < e, 0, qpois(uy, m)),
              if (fam == "poisson") qpois(uy, m) else qbinom(uy, 10, m))
  structure(data.frame(x, y)[seq_len(n), ], d = d)
}

fit <- function(d, fam) if (fam == "poisson") glm(y ~ x, poisson, d) else glm(cbind(y, 10 - y) ~ x, binomial, d)

expl <- c(
  ok    = "The data were simulated from the fitted model's own distribution, so any patterns are due to sampling variation.",
  over  = "The variance is larger than the model assumes. Too many residuals lie near 0 and 1, so in the QQ-plot the points fall below the line on the left and above it on the right, and in the residuals vs predicted plot the outer quantile curves move outwards.",
  under = "The variance is smaller than the model assumes. Too many residuals lie near 0.5, so in the QQ-plot the points lie above the line on the left and below it on the right, and in the residuals vs predicted plot the outer quantile curves move towards 0.5.",
  zero  = "Some counts are zero for a reason the model does not include. The zero-inflation plot shows more zeros than in the simulations, and in the residuals vs predicted plot these zeros have residuals near 0, also where the predicted mean is high.",
  curve = "The true relationship is curved on the link scale, but the model is a straight line on that scale. The quantile curves in the residuals vs predicted plot bend (a U-shape or its reverse).",
  out   = "One observation (number 1) lies far from the others, at an extreme value of \\(x\\). It shows as a single tall spike in the Cook's distance plot. As explained in the video, DHARMa's own outlier test has limitations."
)

tst <- c(over = "disp", under = "disp", zero = "zero", curve = "qu", out = "cook")

tl <- c(ks = "KS test", disp = "dispersion test", out = "outlier test", qu = "combined quantile test",
        zero = "zero-inflation test", cook = "Cook's distance criterion")

flag <- function(p) c(ks = isTRUE(p[["ks"]] < 0.05), disp = isTRUE(p[["disp"]] < 0.05), out = isTRUE(p[["out"]] < 0.05),
                      qu = isTRUE(p[["qu"]] < 0.05), zero = isTRUE(p[["zero"]] < 0.05), cook = isTRUE(p[["cook"]] > 0.5))

pv <- function(p) if (is.na(p)) "n/a" else if (p < 0.001) "\\(p < 0.001\\)" else sprintf("\\(p = %.3f\\)", p)

val <- function(p, k) if (k == "cook") sprintf("\\(D = %.2f\\)", p[["cook"]]) else pv(p[[k]])

cg <- c(over = "disp", under = "disp", zero = "disp")

hard <- function(g, y, f) if (g == "ok") !f[[tst[[y]]]] else
  f[[tst[[g]]]] && (y == "ok" || g == "out" || !f[[tst[[y]]]])

colour <- function(g, y, f) {
  if (g == y) return("blue")
  if (isTRUE(cg[g] == cg[y])) return("partial")
  if (hard(g, y, f)) "orange" else "red"
}

bm <- c(Easy = 15, Medium = 10)

ver <- 1

bench <- function(b, t) {
  r <- diff(cumsum(c(rep(FALSE, 20), b)), 20)
  if (any(r >= t)) return(tagList(span(style = "color: #4393c3;", "✓"), " reached"))
  sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * tail(r, 1) / t)
}

fr <- function(yl, tt) {
  u <- par("usr")
  par(family = "serif")
  mtext(yl, 2, 3, col = "grey10", cex = par("cex"))
  mtext(expression(bold(x)), 1, 3, col = "grey10", cex = par("cex"))
  par(family = "sans")
  mtext(tt, 3, 1, font = 2, cex = par("cex"))
  rect(u[1], u[3], u[2], u[4], col = "grey97", border = NA)
  g <- function(t) seq(t[1] - diff(t[1:2]), t[length(t)] + diff(t[1:2]), diff(t[1:2]) / 2)
  abline(h = g(axTicks(2)), v = g(axTicks(1)), lwd = 2, col = "white")
  abline(h = axTicks(2), v = axTicks(1), lwd = 3, col = "white")
  eaxis(1, col = "grey25", col.axis = "grey25", col.ticks = "grey25", small.args = list(col = "grey25"))
  eaxis(2, col = "grey25", col.axis = "grey25", col.ticks = "grey25", small.args = list(col = "grey25"))
}

dat <- function(e, v) {
  d <- e$d
  po <- e$fam == "poisson"
  m <- fit(d, e$fam)
  tr <- function(x) mu(x, e$fam, e$type, e$lvl, e$sg)
  lk <- if (po) log else qlogis
  r <- range(d$x)
  g <- seq(r[1] - 0.04 * diff(r), r[2] + 0.04 * diff(r), length.out = 200)
  y <- if (po) d$y else d$y / 10
  j <- seq_len(min(3, nrow(d)))
  i <- unique(c(order(-e$cd)[j], which(e$r$u %in% c(0, 1))))
  par(mfrow = if (v) c(2, 1) else c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 5, 3, 3) + 0.1)
  par(cex = 0.83)
  a <- predict(m, data.frame(x = g), type = "response")
  plot(d$x, y, type = "n", bty = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", ylim = range(y, a, tr(g)))
  fr(if (po) expression(bold(y)) else expression(bold(y / 10)), "Response scale")
  lines(g, tr(g), col = "grey", lwd = 3)
  lines(g, a, col = "steelblue", lwd = 3)
  legend("topleft", c("Fitted model", "True relationship"), col = c("steelblue", "grey"), lwd = 3, bty = "n")
  points(d$x, y, pch = 19)
  text(d$x[i], y[i], rownames(d)[i], pos = ifelse(d$x[i] > 0, 2, 4), cex = 0.8)
  b <- predict(m, data.frame(x = g))
  plot(r, range(b, lk(tr(g))), type = "n", bty = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  fr(if (po) expression(bold(log(lambda))) else expression(bold(logit(p))), "Link scale")
  lines(g, lk(tr(g)), col = "grey", lwd = 3)
  lines(g, b, col = "steelblue", lwd = 3)
}

ckd <- function(D) {
  i <- seq_along(D)
  j <- order(-D)[seq_len(min(3, length(D)))]
  plot(i, D, type = "h", axes = FALSE, lwd = 2, lend = 1, las = 1, bty = "n", ylim = c(0, 1.08 * max(D, na.rm = TRUE)),
       xlab = "Observation number", ylab = "")
  mtext("Cook's distance", 2, 3, cex = par("cex"))
  mtext("Cook's distance", 3, 1.25, font = 2, cex = par("cex"))
  axis(1)
  eaxis(2)
  abline(h = 1, col = "red", lty = 3)
  abline(h = 0.5, col = "orange", lty = 3)
  text(j, D[j], j, pos = 3, cex = 0.8, xpd = TRUE)
}

zpl <- function(z, o, v = FALSE) {
  hist(z, xlim = range(z, o), col = "lightgrey", breaks = 50, cex.main = 0.8,
       main = gsub("(.{1,50})(\\s|$)", "\\1\n",
                   "DHARMa zero-inflation test via comparison to expected zeros with simulation under H0 = fitted model"),
       xlab = "")
  title(xlab = paste0("Simulated values, red line = fitted model.", if (v) "\n" else " ", "p-value (two.sided) = ", gp(z, o)),
        line = if (v) 3.2 else 2)
  abline(v = o, lwd = 2, col = "red")
}

dg <- function(e, v) {
  par(mfrow = if (v) c(4, 1) else c(2, 2), mar = c(5, 4, 3, 2) + 0.1, mgp = c(2, 0.75, 0))
  par(cex = 0.83)
  qqp(e$r)
  rvp(e$r)
  ckd(e$cd)
  zpl(e$zs, e$zo, v)
}

js <- "
Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('lock', function(x) {
  $('#guess').toggleClass('locked', x.lock);
  $('input[name=guess], #check').prop('disabled', x.lock);
  $('input[name=guess][value=zero]').prop('disabled', x.lock || !x.zero).closest('label').toggleClass('na', !x.zero);
  $('input[name=view]').prop('disabled', !x.lock);
});
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() {
  var tex = function(el) {
    renderMathInElement(el, {delimiters: [{left: '\\\\(', right: '\\\\)', display: false},
                                          {left: '\\\\[', right: '\\\\]', display: true}], throwOnError: false});
  };
  tex(document.body);
  new MutationObserver(function(ms) {
    ms.forEach(function(m) { if (m.addedNodes.length) tex(m.target); });
  }).observe(document.body, {childList: true, subtree: true});
});
var skey = 'rodenburg-apps:DHARMa-diagnostics:v1';
$(document).on('shiny:connected', function() {
  var ok = false, rec = null;
  try {
    localStorage.setItem(skey + ':test', '1');
    localStorage.removeItem(skey + ':test');
    ok = true;
    rec = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(skey));
  } catch (e) {}
  Shiny.setInputValue('store', {ok: ok, rec: rec});
});
Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('put', function(x) {
  try { localStorage.setItem(skey, JSON.stringify(x)); } catch (e) {}
});
function resetScores() {
  if (confirm('Reset all scores? This cannot be undone.')) Shiny.setInputValue('reset', true, {priority: 'event'});
}
"

kx <-"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/KaTeX/0.16.11/"

sec <- function(t, ...) tags$details(class = "sec", style = "margin-bottom: 0.75em;",
                                     tags$summary(fontawesome::fa("chevron-right", fill = "steelblue"), " ", strong(t)),
                                     div(style = "margin: 0.5em 0 0 1em;", ...))

item <- function(t, ...) tagList(tags$dt(t), tags$dd(style = "margin-bottom: 0.6em;", ...))

sh <- c(ok = "No assumptions violated", over = "Overdispersion", under = "Underdispersion", zero = "Zero-inflation",
        curve = "Non-linearity", out = "Outlier")

grp <- list(" " = list("ok"), "Distribution:" = list(c("over", "under", "zero")),
            "Mean and influence:" = list(c("curve", "out")))

opt <- function(k, first) tags$label(class = "radio-inline",
                                     style = paste0("margin: 0 0 0.25em 0;",
                                                    if (k == "ok") " grid-column: 1 / -1;" else if (first) " grid-column: 1;"),
                                     tags$input(type = "radio", name = "guess", value = k), span(sh[[k]]))

row <- function(k) lapply(seq_along(k), function(i) opt(k[i], i == 1))

guess <- div(id = "guess", class = "form-group shiny-input-radiogroup shiny-input-container", role = "radiogroup",
             `aria-labelledby` = "guess-label", style = "width: auto;",
             tags$label(class = "control-label", id = "guess-label", `for` = "guess", style = "margin-bottom: 0.6em;",
                        "What are you looking at?"),
             div(class = "shiny-options-group",
                 style = "display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, max-content)); column-gap: 1em;",
                 lapply(names(grp), function(g) tagList(
                   if (g != " ") div(style = "grid-column: 1 / -1; margin-top: 0.3em; font-size: 85%; color: grey;", g),
                   lapply(grp[[g]], row)))))

ref <- tagList(
  hr(),
  h3(id = "explanation", "Explanation"),
  p("The sections on statistical terminology and diagnostic plots cover what you should know for this course. ",
    "The section on significance tests goes into more detail than you need, and is merely there for reference."),
  sec("Statistical terminology", tags$dl(
    item("DHARMa residual",
         "DHARMa simulates new possible outcomes from the fitted model many times over (250 by default), conditional on each ",
         "observation's fitted value. In simpler terms, it determines for each observation what the assumed distribution looks ",
         "like, and then looks where the observation falls in its own assumed distribution: the DHARMa residual is the ",
         "proportion of simulated values that are lower than the actual observation. If the assumptions are reasonable, around ",
         "10% of all observations fall in the lowest 10% of their own distribution, around 20% in the lowest 20%, and so on, so ",
         "the DHARMa residuals look like random uniform noise between 0 and 1."),
    item("Universality of the uniform",
         "If you know the CDF (cumulative distribution function) of the distribution that a set of values comes from, applying ",
         "it to those values always results in uniformly distributed values between 0 and 1. The CDF answers the question: what ",
         "proportion of values do you expect up till a certain point? We never know the true distribution, but if all ",
         "assumptions are correct, it is whatever we assumed it to be, with the parameters we estimated. That is the trick ",
         "behind DHARMa: the further the DHARMa residuals deviate from uniformity, the less realistic the assumptions."),
    item("Discrete outcomes",
         "For discrete distributions, such as the Poisson and binomial, the trick still works by adding random uniform noise ",
         "in between possible values on this scale. This app fixes these random numbers, as DHARMa does by default, so a sample ",
         "always gives the same plots."),
    item("Outlier (in DHARMa)",
         "An observation completely outside the range of its simulated values: a DHARMa residual of 0 means that all simulated ",
         "values were larger, and 1 that all were smaller than the actual observation. Outliers are drawn as stars in the ",
         "residuals vs predicted plot. Even if the model is correct, each observation has a chance of up to ",
         "roughly 1% of falling outside at DHARMa's default of 250 simulations, and a larger sample gives more chances. A ",
         "single star is therefore not evidence of a problem."),
    item("Rank-transformed predictions",
         "The horizontal axis of the residuals vs predicted plot: the predictions of the model replaced by their ranks and ",
         "scaled to run from 0 to 1, so that the points are spread evenly."),
    item("Quantile curves",
         "A quantile tells at what point you expect a certain proportion of values: the opposite question to the one the CDF ",
         "answers. The curves in the residuals vs predicted plot are estimated with quantile regression: the bottom curve shows ",
         "where the lowest 25% of DHARMa residuals are, the middle curve the lowest 50%, and the top curve the lowest 75%. The ",
         "grey bands show their uncertainty, and a curve is red if it deviates significantly."),
    item("Dispersion",
         "In most GLMs, the mean and variance are related: for a Poisson distribution the variance equals the mean, and for a ",
         "binomial distribution with \\(n\\) trials it is \\(n p (1 - p)\\). Dispersion compares the variance of the outcome ",
         "with this assumed mean-variance relationship: overdispersion means more variance than the model predicts, ",
         "underdispersion less.",
         " See: ", a(href = "https://fransrodenburg.github.io/Applied-Statistics/GLM.html",
                    target = "_blank", rel = "noopener noreferrer",
                    fontawesome::fa("book", fill = "steelblue"), " Generalized Linear Models"), "."),
    item("Zero-inflation",
         "More zeros than the model predicts, typically because some zeros arise from a separate process, for example sites ",
         "where a species cannot occur at all. In this app, it occurs in Poisson samples only."),
    item("Link scale",
         "A GLM is a straight line on the link scale: \\(\\log(\\lambda)\\) in Poisson regression and \\(\\text{logit}(p)\\) in ",
         "binomial regression. On the scale of the outcome itself, the same model is a curve."),
    item("Cook's distance",
         "A magnitude-based measure of influence, well defined for GLMs: how much the fitted values would change if the ",
         "observation were left out. As in ordinary linear models, a Cook's distance above 0.5 is worth investigating, and ",
         "values above 1 are typically considered influential. In R, it assumes the variance implied by the family, so ",
         "overdispersion inflates it for many observations at once."),
    item("Sampling variation",
         "Differences between samples from the same population that arise by chance alone. It is why ",
         "plots of data that meet every assumption can still show apparent patterns."),
    item("Seed",
         "A number that fixes the random number generator, so that the same sample can be generated again.")
  )),
  sec("Diagnostic plots",
      p("In ordinary linear models, we assume a normal distribution around the line that looks the same at any point, so we ",
        "can compare the residuals to an actual normal distribution. For GLMs, that does not quite work. The assumed ",
        "distribution can be discrete and bounded, whereas residuals are continuous and can be negative. And in most GLMs, the ",
        "mean and variance are related, so the assumed distribution looks different at every point. DHARMa solves this by ",
        "transforming the outcome to a uniform scale: if the DHARMa residuals look like random uniform noise, the assumptions ",
        "held up reasonably well."),
      tags$dl(
        item("QQ-plot residuals",
             "The DHARMa residuals plotted against a true uniform distribution. If the distributional assumption of the model is ",
             "reasonable, the points should more or less follow the straight line. Overdispersion puts the points below the line ",
             "on the left and above it on the right, underdispersion the reverse. Significance tests for deviation (KS test), ",
             "dispersion and outlyingness are included for ease of judgment, in red when \\(p < 0.05\\)."),
        item("DHARMa residual vs. predicted",
             "The DHARMa residuals against the predicted values. This is very similar to a residuals vs fitted plot: moving from ",
             "left to right, you travel up or down the estimated relationship. If the model captures the trend in the data well, ",
             "the quantile curves should not reveal any remaining trend: curvature indicates non-linearity. And if the ",
             "mean-variance relationship holds up, the curves should also not diverge: curves that are further apart than 0.25 and ",
             "0.75, or drift away from each other, mean that the variance is larger than the model predicts (overdispersion); ",
             "curves closer together mean that it is smaller (underdispersion). Stars at the bottom at higher predictions are zeros ",
             "where the model expects larger counts, a sign of zero-inflation."),
        item("Cook's distance",
             "The Cook's distance of each observation against its observation number, with dotted lines at 0.5 (orange) and 1 ",
             "(red). A single spike that towers above the rest indicates an influential observation. Unlike DHARMa's definition of ",
             "an outlier, Cook's distance takes magnitude into account. Many tall spikes at once rather indicate more variance ",
             "than the model assumes."),
        item("Zero-inflation test",
             "A histogram of the number of zeros in each of the 250 simulated data sets, with a red line at the number of zeros in ",
             "the data. A red line far to the right means more zeros than the model expects."),
        item("Resulting model",
             "Available after answering. Left: the data with the fitted model and the true relationship, on the scale of the ",
             "outcome (counts, or the proportion of the 10 trials); observations with large Cook's distances and DHARMa outliers ",
             "are labelled. Right: the same on the link scale, where the fitted model is a straight line. Counts of 0 (and 10 of ",
             "10) have no value on the link scale, so only the lines are shown there.")
      )),
  sec("Difficulty levels",
      p("The difficulty sets the size of the deviation in new samples. The same seed gives the same random ",
        "noise at every level, so you can compare how a deviation looks at different difficulties. To do so, ",
        "enter the seed of the example, change the difficulty and press 'New sample'."),
      tags$dl(
        item("Easy",
             "Large deviations. Learn the typical pattern of each deviation and the plot in which it shows. ",
             "The 'benchmark' is achieved when you answer 15 of the last 20 correct."),
        item("Medium",
             "Clear deviations, closer to what you may encounter in actual data. The 'benchmark' is achieved when you answer 10 of the last 20 correct."),
        item("Hard",
             "Small deviations, not necessarily large enough to be a problem, and much harder to detect consistently."),
        item("Impossible",
             "Subtle deviations, about as large as sampling variation. In small samples, they are practically ",
             "impossible to detect, by eye or by any test.")
      )),
  sec("Significance tests",
      p("After each answer, the app shows the results of five significance tests (flagged when \\(p < 0.05\\)) and one rule ",
        "of thumb on the same sample, so that you can compare your own judgment with what a test would have concluded. A ",
        "significance test asks whether a deviation can be detected in this sample, not whether it is large enough to matter, ",
        "so its result depends strongly on sample size. Checks also respond to deviations they are not meant for: at Easy, ",
        "\\(n = 30\\), strong non-linearity also makes the dispersion test significant in about 6 in 10 Poisson samples."),
      tags$dl(
        item("KS test (Kolmogorov\u2013Smirnov)",
             "The test for deviation in the QQ-plot: it tests whether the DHARMa residuals are uniformly distributed, that is, ",
             "whether the points follow the line. It does not point to a specific deviation. In this app it is very conservative: in 1000 samples without ",
             "a violation, at each sample size and for both families, it never flagged one."),
        item("Dispersion test",
             "Compares the spread of the residuals (observed minus fitted values) with that in the simulated data sets, in ",
             "both directions. It detects over- and underdispersion, but also responds to other deviations. In this app, it ",
             "rarely detects underdispersion in binomial samples: in 3 in 100 at Easy, \\(n = 30\\)."),
        item("Outlier test",
             "Checks how often observations fall outside the range of their simulated values, and whether this matches what you ",
             "would expect given the sample size (using a bootstrap). This definition of an outlier has two major limitations. ",
             "First, whether an observation is flagged depends on the number of simulations: with more simulations, rarer events ",
             "will eventually occur, and the range of simulated values grows wider. In an actual analysis, rerun DHARMa with a ",
             "larger number of simulations and check whether the observation is still flagged (this app always uses 250). ",
             "Second, it ignores magnitude: an observation just outside the simulated range counts as much as one far outside ",
             "it. A single outlier is also rarely flagged: in this app, in fewer than 3 in 100 outlier samples at Easy, ",
             "\\(n = 30\\). Supplement it with a magnitude-based measure, like Cook's distance. The stars in the residuals vs ",
             "predicted plot turn red ",
             "only when a second, independent run of this test is significant, so their colour can disagree with the result in ",
             "the QQ-plot."),
        item("Combined quantile test",
             "Each quantile curve comes with its own test of whether it deviates from 0.25, 0.5 or 0.75. Since this involves ",
             "multiple significance tests, there is an inflated chance of a false positive. DHARMa corrects for this with a ",
             "combined adjusted quantile test (Benjamini\u2013Hochberg adjustment), shown above the plot: only if this test is ",
             "significant were significant problems detected. Even so, in small samples it is significant too often: in this ",
             "app, in about a third of the samples without a ",
             "violation at \\(n = 10\\), one in five at \\(n = 30\\), and fewer than 1 in 10 at \\(n = 100\\)."),
        item("Zero-inflation test",
             "Compares the number of zeros in the data with the numbers in the simulated data sets, in both directions. ",
             "Overdispersion also produces extra zeros, so the test can respond to it: at Easy, \\(n = 30\\), it flagged about 1 ",
             "in 7 overdispersed Poisson samples, against 95 in 100 zero-inflated ones."),
        item("Cook's distance (maximum)",
             "Not a significance test, but a conventional rule of thumb: as in ordinary linear models, values above 0.5 are ",
             "worth investigating, and values above 1 are typically considered influential. In small samples, it is often exceeded even when every assumption holds: at ",
             "\\(n = 10\\), in about 4 to 5 in 10 such samples in this app. In larger samples, a single observation has less ",
             "influence, so at \\(n = 100\\) even a clear outlier often stays below 0.5.")
      ))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  H    <- reactiveVal(list())
  pos  <- reactiveVal(0)
  pend <- reactiveVal(NULL)
  rec  <- reactiveVal(list(lvl = character(0), type = character(0), col = character(0)))
  ld   <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

  put <- function() if (ld()) session$sendCustomMessage("put", c(v = ver, rec()))

  observeEvent(input$store, {
    r <- input$store$rec
    if (is.list(r) && identical(as.numeric(unlist(r$v)), ver)) {
      x <- lapply(list(lvl = r$lvl, type = r$type, col = r$col), function(x) as.character(unlist(x)))
      if (length(unique(lengths(x))) == 1 && all(x$lvl %in% colnames(dif$poisson), x$type %in% names(lab),
                                                  x$col %in% c("blue", "partial", "orange", "red")))
        rec(Map(c, x, rec()))
    }
    ld(TRUE)
    put()
  })

  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    rec(lapply(rec(), `[`, 0))
    put()
  })

  cur    <- reactive(H()[[req(pos())]])
  latest <- reactive(pos() == length(H()))
  lk     <- reactive(!latest() || !is.null(cur()$ans))

  observe({
    req(length(H()) > 0)
    a <- cur()$ans
    s <- if (!is.null(a)) a else if (!lk()) isolate(pend())
    updateRadioButtons(session, "guess", selected = if (is.null(s)) character(0) else s)
    if (!lk()) updateRadioButtons(session, "view", selected = "diag")
    session$sendCustomMessage("lock", list(lock = lk(), zero = cur()$fam == "poisson"))
  })

  observeEvent(input$guess, if (latest() && is.null(cur()$ans)) pend(input$guess))

  observeEvent(input$new, {
    f <- input$fam
    s <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(input$seed))
    if (is.na(s)) {
      h <- Filter(function(e) e$fam == f, H())
      O <- c(table(factor(vapply(h, `[[`, "", "type"), names(w[[f]]))))
      y <- sample(names(w[[f]]), 1, prob = w[[f]] * exp(lam * pmax(0, length(h) * w[[f]] / sum(w[[f]]) - O)))
      S <- sample.int(1e6, 1000)
      s <- c(Find(function(s) scen(s, f) == y, S), S[1])[1]
    }
    type <- scen(s, f)
    d <- sim(input$n, f, type, input$lvl)
    m <- fit(d, f)
    r <- withProgress(message = "Simulating residuals and fitting quantile regressions ...", value = 0.5, dharma(m))
    cd <- unname(cooks.distance(m))
    zs <- as.integer(colSums(r$S == 0))
    zo <- sum(r$y == 0)
    e <- list(seed = s, n = input$n, fam = f, lvl = input$lvl, type = type, sg = attr(d, "d"), d = d,
              r = r[c("f", "u", "q", "g", "M", "pq", "pqa", "p", "out2", "qu")], cd = cd, zs = zs, zo = zo,
              p = c(r$p, qu = r$pqa, zero = gp(zs, zo), cook = max(cd, na.rm = TRUE)), ans = NULL)
    pend(NULL)
    H(c(H(), list(e)))
    pos(length(H()))
    updateTextInput(session, "seed", value = "")
  }, ignoreNULL = FALSE)

  observeEvent(input$prev, pos(max(1, pos() - 1)))
  observeEvent(input$nxt, pos(min(length(H()), pos() + 1)))

  observeEvent(input$check, {
    req(latest(), input$guess, is.null(cur()$ans))
    h <- H()
    h[[pos()]]$ans <- input$guess
    H(h)
    e <- h[[pos()]]
    rec(Map(c, rec(), list(lvl = e$lvl, type = e$type, col = colour(e$ans, e$type, flag(e$p)))))
    put()
  })

  output$pos  <- renderText(sprintf("Example %d of %d", req(pos()), length(H())))
  output$used <- renderUI(tagList(sprintf("%s, %s difficulty, \\(n = %d\\), seed:", fl[[cur()$fam]], cur()$lvl, cur()$n),
                                  span(style = "font-family: monospace;", cur()$seed)))

  output$diag <- renderImage({
    wd <- req(session$clientData$output_diag_width)
    nar <- wd < 600
    dv <- lk() && identical(input$view, "data")
    h <- round(wd * if (dv && nar) 2 else if (dv) 0.45 else if (nar) 3.2 else 0.8)
    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
    svg(f, width = wd / 96, height = h / 96)
    if (dv) dat(cur(), nar) else dg(cur(), nar)
    dev.off()
    list(src = f, width = wd, height = h, contentType = "image/svg+xml")
  }, deleteFile = TRUE)

  output$fb <- renderUI({
    g <- cur()$ans
    if (is.null(g)) return(if (!latest()) div(class = "alert alert-secondary", "Not answered."))
    y <- cur()$type
    p <- cur()$p
    f <- flag(p)
    k <- colour(g, y, f)
    cd <- if (p[["cook"]] > 1) " (influential)" else if (p[["cook"]] > 0.5) " (possibly influential)" else ""
    div(class = paste0("alert fb-", k),
        strong(switch(k, blue = "Correct. ", partial = "Close. ", "Not quite. ")),
        paste0("This was: ", lab[y], ". ", expl[y]),
        if (k == "partial") " You identified the right assumption (the distribution of the outcome), but not the pattern.",
        if (g != y && hard(g, y, f)) {
          if (g == "ok") paste0(" This was a hard example: the ", tl[[tst[[y]]]], " would not have flagged it either (",
                                val(p, tst[[y]]), ").")
          else if (y == "ok") paste0(" This was a hard example: the ", tl[[tst[[g]]]], " also flagged this sample (",
                                     val(p, tst[[g]]), "), although every assumption held.")
          else paste0(" This was a hard example: the ", tl[[tst[[g]]]], " also flagged this sample (",
                      val(p, tst[[g]]), ")",
                      if (!f[[tst[[y]]]]) paste0(", but the ", tl[[tst[[y]]]], " did not (", val(p, tst[[y]]), ")"), ".")
        },
        if (cur()$lvl == "Impossible" && y != "ok")
          " At this level, the deviation is about as visible as sampling noise. Try the same seed at Easy to see it clearly.",
        br(), br(),
        em(style = "font-size: 85%;", sprintf(paste0("KS test %s, dispersion test %s, outlier test %s, combined quantile test %s, ",
                                                     "zero-inflation test %s, max. Cook's distance %s%s."),
                                              pv(p[["ks"]]), pv(p[["disp"]]), pv(p[["out"]]), pv(p[["qu"]]), pv(p[["zero"]]),
                                              val(p, "cook"), cd)))
  })

  output$score <- renderUI({
    k <- rec()$col
    L <- rec()$lvl
    Y <- rec()$type
    dv <- setdiff(unlist(grp), "ok")
    ok <- dv %in% Y[k == "blue"]
    td <- function(...) tags$td(..., style = "text-align: center;")
    th <- function(...) tags$th(..., style = "text-align: center;")
    rw <- function(t, i, b, ...) tags$tr(..., tags$td(t),
                                         td(sprintf("%d of %d (%.0f%%)", sum(k[i] == "blue"), sum(i), 100 * mean(k[i] == "blue"))),
                                         td(sum(k[i] == "partial")),
                                         td(sum(k[i] == "orange")),
                                         td(b))
    l <- intersect(colnames(dif$poisson), L)
    rows <- if (!length(l)) tags$tr(tags$td(colspan = 5, style = "color: grey;", "No answers yet")) else
      c(lapply(l, function(l) rw(if (l == "Impossible") em(l) else l, L == l,
                                  if (l %in% names(bm)) bench(k[L == l] == "blue", bm[[l]]) else "–")),
        if (length(l) > 1) list(rw("Total", rep(TRUE, length(k)), "", style = "border-top: 2px solid #ddd;")))
    tagList(
      h4("Results"),
      div(style = "overflow-x: auto;", tags$table(class = "table table-condensed",
                                                  tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Difficulty"), th("Correct"),
                                                                     th("Close"), th("Hard (orange)"),
                                                                     th("Benchmark"))),
                                                  tags$tbody(rows))),
      p(style = "margin-bottom: 0.25em;", sprintf("Deviations identified (%d of %d):", sum(ok), length(dv))),
      div(id = "dev", style = "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; column-gap: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em;",
          lapply(seq_along(dv), function(j) if (ok[j]) span(span(style = "color: #4393c3;", "✓"), " ", sh[[dv[j]]]) else
            span(style = "color: grey;", sh[[dv[j]]]))),
      p(style = "font-size: 85%; color: grey;",
        "Close: the right assumption (the distribution of the outcome), but the wrong pattern.", br(),
        "Hard (orange): wrong answers for which the checks pointed to your answer rather than to the correct one.", br(),
        sprintf("Always answering '%s' would give about %.0f%% correct at any level.",
                lab["ok"], 100 * w$poisson[["ok"]] / sum(w$poisson))),
      if (length(k)) tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-default btn-sm", onclick = "resetScores()",
                                 "Reset scores"))
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

name: dharma.R
content:
# Reimplementation of DHARMa 0.5.0 (simulateResiduals + plot) for glm objects
# (Poisson; binomial with 0/1, cbind(k, m - k) or weights). Equal RNG consumption,
# in the order of plot.DHARMa: residuals (own seed, state restored), KS test,
# outlier test (QQ panel), dispersion test, outlier test (point colours), 3 x qgam.

gp <- function(s, o) min(min(mean(s <= o), mean(s >= o)) * 2, 1)

rk <- function(x) {
  r <- rank(x, ties.method = "average")
  r / max(r)
}

pit <- function(S, y) {
  lo <- unname(rowMeans(S < y))
  up <- unname(rowMeans(S <= y))
  if (any(lo != up)) runif(length(lo), lo, up) else lo
}

obs <- function(m) {
  F <- model.frame(m)
  y <- F[, 1]
  if (is.factor(y)) y <- as.numeric(y) - 1
  if (family(m)$family == "binomial" && "(weights)" %in% colnames(F)) y <- y * F[["(weights)"]]
  if (is.matrix(y)) y <- if (ncol(y) == 1) as.vector(y) else y[, 1]
  y
}

sims <- function(m, B) {
  S <- simulate(m, nsim = B)
  F <- model.frame(m)
  if (family(m)$family == "binomial") {
    if (is.factor(S[[1]])) S <- data.matrix(S) - 1
    if ("(weights)" %in% colnames(F)) S <- S * F[["(weights)"]]
    else if (is.matrix(S[[1]])) S <- as.matrix(S)[, seq(1, 2 * B, by = 2), drop = FALSE]
  }
  if (!is.matrix(S)) S <- data.matrix(S)
  S
}

res <- function(m, y, B, seed) {
  e <- globalenv()
  r0 <- if (exists(".Random.seed", e, inherits = FALSE)) get(".Random.seed", e)
  on.exit(if (is.null(r0)) rm(".Random.seed", envir = e) else assign(".Random.seed", r0, envir = e))
  set.seed(seed)
  if (is.null(r0)) runif(1)
  S <- sims(m, B)
  list(S = S, u = pit(S, y))
}

otest <- function(S, u, nb) {
  n <- nrow(S)
  B <- ncol(S)
  if (n > 500) {
    k <- sum(u < 1 / (B + 1)) + sum(u > 1 - 1 / (B + 1))
    return(binom.test(k, n, p = 1 / (B + 1) * 2)$p.value)
  }
  nb <- min(nb, B)
  o <- mean(u == 0) + mean(u == 1)
  b <- rep(NA, nb)
  for (i in seq_len(nb)) {
    r <- pit(S[, sample(seq_len(B)[-i], size = B, replace = TRUE), drop = FALSE], S[, i])
    b[i] <- mean(r == 1) + mean(r == 0)
  }
  gp(b, o)
}

qtest <- function(u, f, qu) {
  q <- rk(f)
  d <- data.frame(res = u, pred = q)
  g <- data.frame(pred = sort(q))
  k <- min(length(unique(q)), 10)
  nq <- length(qu)
  pq <- rep(NA, nq)
  M <- matrix(NA, nrow(d), 2 * nq)
  for (i in seq_len(nq)) {
    dt <- d
    dt$res <- dt$res - qu[i]
    z <- try(capture.output(fit <- qgam::qgam(res ~ s(pred, k = k), data = dt, qu = qu[i])), silent = TRUE)
    if (!inherits(z, "try-error")) {
      s <- summary(fit)
      pq[i] <- min(p.adjust(c(s$p.table[1, 4], s$s.table[1, 4]), method = "BH"))
      h <- predict(fit, newdata = g, se.fit = TRUE)
      M[, 2 * i - 1] <- h$fit + qu[i]
      M[, 2 * i] <- 1.96 * h$se.fit
    }
  }
  list(q = q, g = g$pred, pq = pq, pqa = min(p.adjust(pq, method = "BH")), M = M)
}

dharma <- function(m, B = 250, nb = 100, qu = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), seed = 123) {
  y <- obs(m)
  f <- as.vector(predict(m, type = "response"))
  R <- res(m, y, B, seed)
  S <- R$S
  u <- R$u
  ks <- suppressWarnings(ks.test(u, "punif"))$p.value
  o1 <- otest(S, u, nb)
  v <- sd(S)^2
  sp <- function(x) var(x - f) / v
  dp <- gp(apply(S, 2, sp), sp(y))
  o2 <- otest(S, u, nb)
  c(list(y = y, f = f, S = S, u = u, qu = qu,
         p = c(ks = ks, disp = dp, out = o1), out2 = o2),
    qtest(u, f, qu))
}

qqp <- function(r) {
  n <- length(r$u)
  p <- r$p
  plot((1:n) / (n + 1), sort(r$u), pch = 2, las = 1, bty = "n", axes = FALSE,
       xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Expected", ylab = "Observed",
       panel.first = abline(0, 1, col = "red"))
  sfsmisc::eaxis(1, cex.axis = 0.8)
  sfsmisc::eaxis(2, cex.axis = 0.8)
  fp <- sprintf("%.3f", signif(p, 3))
  text(0.33, 0.9, bquote("KS test: p =" ~ .(fp[1])),
       col = if (p[["ks"]] < 0.05) "red" else "grey50", cex = 0.9, xpd = TRUE)
  text(0.5, 0.5, bquote("Dispersion test: p =" ~ .(fp[2])),
       col = if (p[["disp"]] < 0.05) "red" else "grey50", cex = 0.9, xpd = TRUE)
  text(0.67, 0.1, bquote("Outlier test: p =" ~ .(fp[3])),
       col = if (p[["out"]] < 0.05) "red" else "grey50", cex = 0.9, xpd = TRUE)
  s <- any(p < 0.05)
  mtext("QQ-plot residuals", 3, 1.25, font = 2, cex = par("cex"))
  mtext(if (s) "Significant problems detected" else "No significant problems detected",
        3, 0.25, col = if (s) "red" else "grey50", cex = 0.75 * par("cex"))
}

rvp <- function(r) {
  qu <- r$qu
  o <- r$u == 0 | r$u == 1
  cl <- if (r$out2 < 0.05) ifelse(o, "red", "black") else "black"
  plot(r$q, r$u, pch = ifelse(o, 8, 1), col = cl, las = 1, bty = "n", axes = FALSE,
       xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xlab = "Model predictions (rank transformed)", ylab = "",
       panel.first = abline(h = qu, lty = 3, col = "grey75"))
  mtext("DHARMa residual", 2, 3, cex = par("cex"))
  for (i in seq_along(qu)) if (!is.na(r$pq[i])) {
    a <- r$M[, 2 * i - 1]
    b <- r$M[, 2 * i]
    polygon(c(r$g, rev(r$g)), c(a - b, rev(a + b)), border = NA, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.1))
    lines(r$g, a, col = if (r$pq[i] < 0.05) "red" else "black", lwd = 2, lend = 1)
  }
  sfsmisc::eaxis(1, cex.axis = 0.8)
  sfsmisc::eaxis(2, at = seq(0, 1, 0.25), cex.axis = 0.8)
  if (is.na(r$pqa)) {
    l <- "Some quantile regressions failed"
  } else if (any(r$pq < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)) {
    l <- paste0("Quantile deviations detected (red curves)\nCombined adjusted quantile test ",
                if (r$pqa < 0.05) "significant" else "n.s.")
  } else {
    l <- "No significant problems detected"
  }
  s <- l != "No significant problems detected"
  mtext("DHARMa residual vs. predicted", 3, 1.25 + 0.5 * grepl("\n", l), font = 2, cex = par("cex"))
  mtext(l, 3, 0.25, col = if (s) "red" else "grey50", cex = 0.75 * par("cex"))
}

dplot <- function(r, v = FALSE) {
  op <- par(mfrow = if (v) c(2, 1) else c(1, 2), mar = c(5, 4, 3, 2) + 0.1, mgp = c(2, 0.75, 0))
  on.exit(par(op))
  qqp(r)
  rvp(r)
}
